jurisdiction: Cook County (every Cook County voter, including all of Chicago)
number: Cook County advisory question: Millionaire Amendment for Property Tax Relief and Education
official_title: Shall Illinois adopt the Millionaire Amendment for Property Tax Relief and Education, which would enact a 3% income tax surcharge only on millionaires and use 50% of this new revenue to provide property tax relief for residential and commercial taxpayers and 50% to improve state funding for public education?
plain_summary: An advisory poll of Cook County voters. It asks whether Illinois should add a 3% extra income tax on millionaires and split the money: half to cut property taxes for homes and businesses, half to raise state school funding. Your vote sends a message to state leaders; it does not create the tax.
yes_means: You are telling state leaders you support a 3% income tax surcharge on millionaires, with the money split between property tax relief and school funding.
no_means: You are telling state leaders you oppose that surcharge.
fiscal_impact: None directly. Advisory questions do not raise or spend money. The question does not estimate how much the surcharge would raise.
pass_threshold: Simple majority, but advisory only: the result is not binding either way.
confusing_wording_note: It reads like a decision ('Shall Illinois adopt...'), but only Cook County votes on it and it is advisory. Changing the state income tax would take action by the legislature and, for a constitutional amendment, a statewide vote; this ballot cannot do either. The question also does not define 'millionaire' (for example, income over $1 million a year versus net worth). Chicago voters will see a second, similar millionaire question from Chicago Public Schools further down the ballot; they are separate questions.

number: Chicago advisory question: Restart Chicago Gunshot Detection
official_title: Should the City of Chicago restart the use of gunshot detection technology that informs first responders when gunshots are detected?
plain_summary: An advisory poll asking whether Chicago should bring back technology that detects gunfire and alerts police and other first responders. Chicago used a system called ShotSpotter until Mayor Brandon Johnson ended it over concerns about its accuracy; no replacement has been approved.
yes_means: You want the city to start using gunshot detection technology again. The vote is advisory and does not restart it by itself.
no_means: You do not want the city to restart gunshot detection technology. The vote is advisory.
current_law: Chicago is not using gunshot detection technology. Mayor Brandon Johnson discontinued ShotSpotter due to concerns about the program's accuracy and said he would look for a replacement; FOX 32 reports no replacement has been approved or implemented.
fiscal_impact: None directly (advisory). The question does not name a vendor or a cost.
pass_threshold: Simple majority, but advisory only: the result is not binding either way.
confusing_wording_note: The question never names ShotSpotter, the system Chicago used before; 'gunshot detection technology' could mean any vendor. It is advisory, so the City Council and mayor decide what actually happens.

number: Chicago advisory question: Permanent Chicago Festival Space
official_title: Should Chicago develop a permanent festival and outdoor event space for large-scale events?
plain_summary: An advisory poll asking whether Chicago should build a permanent outdoor venue for big festivals and events. The question names no location, cost or funding source.
yes_means: You support Chicago developing a permanent festival and outdoor event space. The vote is advisory.
no_means: You do not support developing a permanent festival space. The vote is advisory.
fiscal_impact: None directly (advisory). No cost, site or funding source is stated on the ballot.
pass_threshold: Simple majority, but advisory only: the result is not binding either way.
confusing_wording_note: The ballot gives no site, price tag or who would pay. A YES is a vote for the general idea only.

number: Chicago advisory question: Chicago Cost Recovery from Midway Blitz
official_title: Shall the City of Chicago pursue all lawful means to recover financial compensation from the federal government for the costs and economic harm caused by the Donald Trump administration's violent, militarized ICE operations, including the Midway Blitz operation led by Greg Bovino, to recover lost tax revenue, public safety response costs, and services provided to residents and families affected by those operations?
plain_summary: An advisory poll asking whether the City of Chicago should try, by any legal means (such as claims or lawsuits), to get the federal government to pay Chicago back for costs tied to federal immigration enforcement in the city, including the operation the question calls 'Midway Blitz.' The costs it lists are lost tax revenue, public safety response, and services for affected residents and families.
yes_means: You want the city to pursue compensation from the federal government for costs tied to these immigration enforcement operations. The vote is advisory.
no_means: You do not want the city to pursue that compensation. The vote is advisory.
fiscal_impact: None directly (advisory). The question gives no dollar estimate of the costs or of what pursuing them would cost.
pass_threshold: Simple majority, but advisory only: the result is not binding either way.
confusing_wording_note: The wording includes descriptions ('violent, militarized') that are the question writers' characterization, not neutral ballot language. What you are actually deciding is narrower: whether the city should try to recover costs from the federal government. It is advisory, so it does not file a lawsuit or spend money on its own.

jurisdiction: Chicago Public Schools District 299 (every Chicago voter)
number: CPS advisory question regarding millionaires surcharge
official_title: Shall Illinois use revenue from a surcharge on millionaires to increase funding to public schools?
plain_summary: An advisory poll of Chicago voters asking whether Illinois should put money from an extra tax on millionaires toward public schools.
yes_means: You are telling state leaders you support using a millionaire surcharge to raise school funding. The vote is advisory.
no_means: You are telling state leaders you oppose that idea. The vote is advisory.
fiscal_impact: None directly (advisory). The question gives no rate or dollar amount.
pass_threshold: Simple majority, but advisory only: the result is not binding either way.
confusing_wording_note: This is a different question from the Cook County 'Millionaire Amendment' question higher on the same ballot. The county one names a 3% rate and splits money between property tax relief and schools; this CPS one names no rate and is about schools only. Both are advisory. The question does not define 'millionaire.'

jurisdiction: Chicago Public Schools District 299 (every Chicago voter)
number: CPS advisory question regarding Chicago land owners
official_title: Should the City of Chicago require owners of long-term vacant or undeveloped commercial or investment properties to pay an additional annual charge that would support Chicago Public Schools?
plain_summary: An advisory poll asking whether the city should charge owners of commercial or investment properties that sit vacant or undeveloped for a long time an extra yearly fee, with the money going to Chicago Public Schools.
yes_means: You support an extra annual charge on long-term vacant or undeveloped commercial and investment properties to help fund CPS. The vote is advisory.
no_means: You oppose that charge. The vote is advisory.
fiscal_impact: None directly (advisory). No amount, rate or definition of 'long-term' is given.
pass_threshold: Simple majority, but advisory only: the result is not binding either way.
confusing_wording_note: The question does not say how long 'long-term' is, how big the charge would be, or how it would be collected. It covers commercial or investment properties, not owner-occupied homes. It is advisory; the City Council would have to create any such charge.

jurisdiction: Proposed Mid-Northside Expanded Mental Health Services Program Area (only voters inside this territory)
official_title: Shall there be established, to serve the territory commonly described on this ballot or notice of this question, a Mid-Northside Expanded Mental Health Services Program, to provide direct free mental health services for any resident of the territory who needs assistance in overcoming or coping with mental or emotional disorders, where such program will be funded through an increase of not more than .025% of the equalized assessed valuation of all properties within the boundaries of the territory?
plain_summary: A binding vote, only for people who live inside the proposed territory (a Mid-North Side area; exact boundaries are printed on the ballot only for voters inside it). It would create a local program offering free mental health care to any resident of the area, paid for by a new property tax of up to 0.025% of the taxable (equalized assessed) value of property in the area. That is at most $25 a year for every $100,000 of equalized assessed value on a tax bill. Under state law (405 ILCS 22/15), if it passes the Governor appoints five commissioners and the Mayor four, most of them residents of the area, to run the program.
yes_means: The program is created and can levy a property tax of up to 0.025% on property in the territory to provide free mental health services to residents.
no_means: The program is not created and no new property tax is levied for it.
current_law: No expanded mental health services program serves this territory today. State law (405 ILCS 22/15) lets a territory inside Chicago create one by referendum, placed on the ballot by City Council resolution or by a petition of voters in the territory; the ballot language follows the form set in that law.
fiscal_impact: New property tax of not more than 0.025% of equalized assessed value (EAV) on all property in the territory: up to $25 a year per $100,000 of EAV. EAV is the taxable value printed on your bill, usually well below market value. A companion question sets the first-year (2027 levy) cap at $1,300,000.
pass_threshold: Simple majority of voters in the territory (binding).
confusing_wording_note: This is one of TWO linked questions. This one asks whether to create the program and its maximum tax rate; the next one asks voters to approve a dollar cap for its first-year tax levy under the state's property tax cap law. The ballot does not say what happens if one passes and the other fails. 'Equalized assessed valuation' is the taxable value on a property tax bill, not the home's sale price. The exact boundary is printed on the ballot only for voters inside the territory; if it is too long, state law says it goes on a large notice posted in the polling place. Our sources do not say which neighborhoods the territory covers.

jurisdiction: Proposed Mid-Northside Expanded Mental Health Services Program Area (only voters inside this territory)
number: 2027 Property Tax Extension: Mid-Northside Expanded Mental Health Services
official_title: Under the Property Tax Extension Limitation Law, may an aggregate extension not to exceed $1,300,000 be made for the Mid-Northside Expanded Mental Health Services Program for the 2027 levy year?
plain_summary: A binding companion question for the same territory. Illinois' property tax cap law (PTELL) requires voters to approve how much a new taxing program may collect in its first year. This sets the Mid-Northside program's total tax levy for the 2027 levy year at no more than $1,300,000.
yes_means: The program may levy up to $1,300,000 in property taxes for the 2027 levy year.
no_means: The $1,300,000 first-year levy is not approved.
current_law: Under the Property Tax Extension Limitation Law, a taxing body's levy is capped; a new program needs voter approval for its first aggregate extension.
fiscal_impact: Up to $1,300,000 in total property taxes for the 2027 levy year, spread across all property in the territory.
pass_threshold: Simple majority of voters in the territory (binding).
confusing_wording_note: 'Aggregate extension' means the total property tax the program can collect that year. 'Property Tax Extension Limitation Law' is the state's tax cap law. This question only matters if the program is created by the question just before it; the ballot does not explain what happens if the two results differ.

number: 4th Ward advisory question: Jesse Jackson Monument Statue
official_title: through referendum that to become a city ordinance supported by the city do hereby petition that the question, should at least a life-size statue of the likeness of Jesse Lewis Jackson Sr. sitting on a monument to be placed in the median at approximately 4946 South Drexel, Chicago Illinois be a public policy to place on the ballot and submitted to the voters of the fourth (4th) ward for their approval or disapproval by referendum at the General Election to be held on November 3rd 2026. This initiative is to become realized by November 2027. This proposal should give homage to a great American Patriot and a token symbol of America's appreciation.
plain_summary: An advisory poll for 4th Ward voters only. It asks whether a statue of Rev. Jesse Lewis Jackson Sr., at least life-size and on a monument, should be placed in the street median near 4946 S. Drexel Blvd., with a goal of November 2027.
yes_means: You support placing a Jesse Jackson statue in the median near 4946 S. Drexel. The vote is advisory.
no_means: You do not support placing the statue there. The vote is advisory.
fiscal_impact: Not stated. The question does not say who would pay for the statue.
pass_threshold: Simple majority, but advisory only: the result is not binding either way.
confusing_wording_note: The printed text is the petition's own run-on wording, so the question is buried in the middle. Strip it down and it asks: should a life-size or larger statue of Jesse Jackson Sr. be placed in the median near 4946 S. Drexel? Despite the phrase 'to become a city ordinance,' this is a non-binding public policy question; the City Council would still have to act.

number: 26th Ward advisory question: Shared Housing Limits in 26th Ward
official_title: Shall new shared housing units be limited in the 26th Ward to help address Chicago's severe rental housing shortage?
plain_summary: An advisory poll for 26th Ward voters only, asking whether new 'shared housing units' should be limited in the ward to help with the city's rental shortage. 'Shared housing unit' is the term Chicago's city code uses for short-term rentals, such as apartments rented by the night on Airbnb or Vrbo.
yes_means: You support limiting new shared housing units (short-term rentals) in the 26th Ward. The vote is advisory.
no_means: You do not support new limits on shared housing units in the ward. The vote is advisory.
pass_threshold: Simple majority, but advisory only: the result is not binding either way.
confusing_wording_note: The ballot does not explain that 'shared housing' means short-term rentals (Airbnb-style), not roommates or group homes. It also does not say what kind of limit or how strict. Advisory only.

jurisdiction: City of Chicago, 7th Ward, 13th Precinct only
number: 7th Ward, Precinct 13 advisory question: Chicago Lakefront National Park
official_title: Shall the City of Chicago support the nomination of a Chicago Lakefront National Park, consisting of all of Chicago's park and public lands adjacent to Lake Michigan including their harbors, lagoons, and inlets?
plain_summary: An advisory poll for one precinct, asking whether the city should support nominating all of Chicago's lakefront parks and public land, including harbors, lagoons and inlets, to become a national park.
yes_means: You want the city to support nominating Chicago's lakefront as a national park. The vote is advisory.
no_means: You do not want the city to support that nomination. The vote is advisory.
pass_threshold: Simple majority, but advisory only: the result is not binding either way.
confusing_wording_note: Only voters in one precinct (7th Ward, Precinct 13) see this. It asks only whether the city should support a nomination; it does not create a park.

jurisdiction: City of Chicago: 7th Ward Precinct 14, 10th Ward Precinct 2, and 10th Ward Precinct 4 only
number: Precinct advisory question: Ensure Remediation of Former South Works Site
official_title: Shall governmental bodies in Illinois ensure the complete and transparent remediation of the former South Works site?
plain_summary: An advisory poll for three Southeast Side precincts, asking whether government agencies in Illinois should make sure the former South Works site is fully and openly cleaned up ('remediation' means environmental cleanup).
yes_means: You want government agencies to ensure a complete, transparent cleanup of the former South Works site. The vote is advisory.
no_means: You do not support that call. The vote is advisory.
pass_threshold: Simple majority, but advisory only: the result is not binding either way.
confusing_wording_note: 'Remediation' means environmental cleanup. Voters in these precincts get a second South Works question right after this one about spending public money on a quantum facility and data center at the same site; the two are voted on separately.

jurisdiction: City of Chicago: 7th Ward Precinct 14, 10th Ward Precinct 2, and 10th Ward Precinct 4 only
number: Precinct advisory question: Government support for Quantum Facility and Data Center at Former South Works Site
official_title: Shall governmental bodies in Illinois spend an estimated $1 billion of taxpayer money to support a quantum facility and data center on the former South Works site?
plain_summary: An advisory poll for three Southeast Side precincts, asking whether government agencies in Illinois should spend an estimated $1 billion in public money to support a quantum computing facility and data center planned for the former South Works site.
yes_means: You support spending an estimated $1 billion in public money on the quantum facility and data center. The vote is advisory.
no_means: You oppose spending that public money on the project. The vote is advisory and does not stop the project.
fiscal_impact: None directly (advisory). The $1 billion figure is the question's own estimate; the ballot does not say where it comes from or which governments would pay.
pass_threshold: Simple majority, but advisory only: the result is not binding either way.
confusing_wording_note: The '$1 billion' is an estimate written into the question, with no source on the ballot. The vote is advisory: a NO does not cancel the project and a YES does not approve any spending.

jurisdiction: City of Chicago: 5th Ward Precincts 1 and 14; 8th Ward Precincts 23, 26 and 27; 21st Ward Precinct 25; 24th Ward Precincts 5, 6 and 12 only
number: Precinct advisory question: 500+ employee Corporate Tax for Youth Jobs and Social Services
official_title: Shall our Alderperson vote to pass a tax on big corporations that have 500 or more employees (would not apply to grocery stores or non profits), in order to fund youth jobs, public mental healthcare, and violence prevention services.
plain_summary: An advisory poll for nine precincts on the South and West Sides. It asks whether your alderperson should vote for a city tax on companies with 500 or more employees (not grocery stores or nonprofits), with the money going to youth jobs, public mental health care and violence prevention.
yes_means: You want your alderperson to vote for a tax on corporations with 500+ employees to fund youth jobs, mental health care and violence prevention. The vote is advisory.
no_means: You do not want your alderperson to vote for that tax. The vote is advisory.
fiscal_impact: None directly (advisory). The question gives no tax rate or amount.
pass_threshold: Simple majority, but advisory only: the result is not binding either way.
confusing_wording_note: No tax rate, amount or method (per employee, per profit, etc.) is given. It only shows up in nine specific precincts. Advisory: it instructs no one.

jurisdiction: City of Chicago, 21st Ward, 10th Precinct only (as the precinct existed at the last general election)
number: Local option: Continue to prohibit retail alcohol sales in Ward 21, Precinct 10
official_title: Shall the prohibition of the sale at retail of alcoholic liquor be continued in the 10th Precinct of the 21st Ward of the City of Chicago (as such precinct existed as of the last general election)?
plain_summary: A binding vote for one precinct that is currently 'dry' (stores there can't sell alcohol). It asks whether to keep that ban.
yes_means: The ban stays. Stores in this precinct still can't sell alcohol.
no_means: The ban ends. Businesses in the precinct could seek city liquor licenses to sell alcohol.
current_law: Retail sale of alcoholic liquor is prohibited in this precinct.
pass_threshold: Simple majority of voters in the precinct (binding local option question).
confusing_wording_note: Flip alert: YES means keep the alcohol ban; NO means end it. The question applies to the precinct's boundaries as of the last general election, which may not match today's precinct exactly.
